title: AI Slop Reputation Carnival
oneLiner: A playful portfolio piece where creators test whether their video/channel looks human-made, lazy, or unfairly suspicious.
targetUser: Creators, editors, students, and portfolio reviewers who want a shareable way to discuss AI-slop perception without turning it into a dry compliance checklist.
keyUx: A carnival-style booth scores a channel concept across human-effort signals, slop smells, disclosure clarity, and audience trust, then produces a funny share card plus serious fixes.
requiredUiSections: Ticket-booth input for channel niche, workflow, assets, voice, editing, and disclosure
Reputation midway with meters for human effort, repetition, originality, and viewer suspicion
“Jury of viewers” reaction cards with skeptical, supportive, and confused audience personas
Fix-it prize wall with concrete improvements ranked by impact
Before/after poster generator for shareable social cards
Tiny serious footer explaining that the score is a perception exercise, not platform policy advice
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app prototype for “AI Slop Reputation Carnival,” a playful diagnostic booth for creators worried their videos look AI-made or low-effort. Include: ticket-booth input, reputation midway meters, viewer jury cards, fix-it prize wall, before/after poster generator, and a small serious disclaimer footer. Design direction: use the playful-experimental profile with bold carnival energy, expressive cards, tactile meters, lively but legible colors, and meme-ready share output; keep it polished enough for a portfolio piece, not childish.
